one_line_contribution: The claim that a large share of agent-memory harm is caused by *when* retrieved experience is seen rather than by its content or volume — operationalized as commit-then-consult (draft and log an answer with no memory, then revise against the identical k=7 items at matched deciding-pass tokens) — plus the risky corollary that GEPA-optimized instructions make memory-first injection *more* harmful because a better instruction is a better prior to abandon.
closest_prior_work: The proposal concedes CoVe and Astute-RAG and implements them (A5), but it never engages the context-vs-parametric knowledge-conflict line, which is where its actual mechanism already lives: Xie et al., 'Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth' (ICLR 2024), shows LLMs flip to coherent external evidence and that eliciting the model's own answer before showing the evidence systematically changes flip behaviour; Zhou et al.'s context-faithful prompting (opinion-based/counterfactual framing) manipulates exactly the 'is this a command or evidence' distinction; GenRead (Yu et al. 2023) is generate-before-retrieve. Together these establish commitment-order-before-evidence as a known lever with known effects. That does not fully collide — none of them is in an agentic loop with an ExpeL-style procedural bank, none decomposes fixes vs. breaks, and none touches instruction optimization — but it does mean the ordering half of the paper is a domain transplant of a documented effect, not a new mechanism. Novelty then rests almost entirely on P4, and the proposal's own refutation clause concedes that if A5 ties A2, nothing but P4 survives.
strongest_objection: Assay sensitivity. The pilot the whole proposal is built on reports the bank fixing *zero* items and breaking six to seven. If the frozen bank behaves the same way (and the write path is unchanged from ExpeL-style distillation), then A0 dominates every memory condition by construction, the P2 non-inferiority test has a 2-point margin around a reference effect of ~0 — a vacuous test that any inert method passes — and 'A2 halves breaks' becomes indistinguishable from 'A2 taught the agent to ignore the bank', which is the outcome the proposal itself calls 'no better than not retrieving.' The dev precheck (≥4% wrong→right) is explicitly 'reported, not used as a gate in silence', i.e. not a gate at all, so the grid can run and produce a headline that is uninterpretable. Second, the two mechanism arms are confounded in ways that let the competing account explain a positive result: G3 changes slot AND removes directive content from the memory slot ('the memory slot retains episodic residue only'), so G3's memory slot carries fewer tokens than A1's — that is A7's volume remedy wearing a slot costume, and P5's 'redundancy' would then be a token-count result. Relatedly, I* is presumably much longer and more specific than the base instruction, so G1 vs. A1 differs in total context length: the token-matching the paper's whole rhetoric depends on is enforced in the memory slot and abandoned in the instruction slot, precisely in the arm carrying the sharpest claim. Third, P4's endpoint is unnormalized: breaks are items correct in the reference and wrong under treatment, so if I* raises G0 accuracy at all, more items become eligible to break and the DiD rises with no change in per-item override hazard — a base-rate artifact that would produce the predicted ≥1.5× ratio for free. The most likely interleaving is the fatal one: A7 ≈ A5 ≈ A2 ≈ A0 on breaks, fixes ≈ 0 everywhere, G1−G0 inflated by G0's higher accuracy — at which point the paper's recommendation is 'retrieve less, or don't retrieve', for 2× the calls.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the dev precheck a hard pre-registered gate with a declared fallback (e.g. gold-trajectory-seeded or task-matched bank) and state in advance that a ≈0-fix bank reframes the paper as 'memory is net-negative in this setting', not as 'our fix preserves fixes'; a non-inferiority margin must be smaller than the reference effect it guards. (2) Report breaks as a hazard conditional on reference-correct instances (breaks / #correct-in-reference) for every fix/break table, and re-state P4 on that normalized quantity — otherwise the interaction is confounded with G0's accuracy. (3) Repair G3 so that slot is varied without varying volume: keep memory-slot token count and item count identical to A1 (pad with the episodic residue, or duplicate the directives into the instruction while leaving the memory slot untouched), and add an instruction control matched to I* in length and directiveness but not GEPA-optimized, so P4 tests optimization rather than instruction verbosity. (4) Sample ≥3 GEPA instruction draws (the Pareto frontier is already there and this is nearly free relative to the 22.5k-episode budget) — a single I* makes P4 an n=1 result the proposal itself flags but does not fix. (5) Add the directiveness manipulation rather than only the directiveness regression: minimal-edit imperative→declarative rewrites of the *same* items at matched tokens. That is the clean, cheap causal test of the paper's own mechanism and it is currently the only one missing.
missing_baseline: Two. (a) A length- and directiveness-matched *unoptimized* instruction in the coupling arm (call it I_len: hand-written or a mid-run GEPA candidate, same token count and imperative density as I*, no training signal). Without it, P4 cannot separate 'the optimizer made the prior stronger' from 'the instruction slot got longer and more imperative', and G1 vs. A1 is not token-matched at all. (b) A placebo-memory arm: k=7 topically plausible but non-applicable items at matched tokens. The override signature (P6, >25% first-action divergence with sub-baseline conditional accuracy) is currently consistent with generic distraction by any instruction-shaped text; without a placebo there is no evidence that the agent is abandoning a correct plan *because the retrieved item is directive about this task*. A6's query-conditioned rewriting does not serve either role.
preprint_collision: Above average and clearly executed — it names ~12 specific recent preprints with IDs, gives a per-item collide/no-collide verdict, concedes CoVe as the structural ancestor, and converts two named competitors (Astute-RAG→A5, MemHarness→A6) into run conditions rather than prose distinctions. I found no 2026 agent-memory preprint in the listed set that already makes the ordering claim, and P4 does look unclaimed. But the check is lopsided in exactly the direction that matters: it sweeps the 2026 agentic-memory axis thoroughly and never sweeps the context-vs-parametric knowledge-conflict axis (Xie et al. ICLR 2024; context-faithful prompting; generate-before-retrieve), which is where 'elicit the model's own answer before showing conflicting evidence' is already an established manipulation with published effects — that is a stronger threat to the ordering half than anything in cluster (3) or (4). The proposal also self-reports that the OpenReview/ACL-EMNLP proceedings sweep for ordering-ablation appendices was never run, and concedes 'a nontrivial probability' that draft-then-consult appears as an appendix ablation somewhere; and P4's unclaimed status rests on 'no paper we found asks', an absence-of-evidence from a search the proposal itself calls budget-exhausted. Honest, but the honesty documents the gap rather than closing it, and the unsearched region is the one containing the closest prior art.
